title: Choose the visual world for the Highland Creative concept
question: The roll assigned The Highlands Show Schedule. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Highlands Show Schedule
options.lineage: Southern Highlands country show prize schedules, entry tags and pavilion ribbons
options.thesis: Forty years of work entered, classed and judged like a show pavilion, and the clients are the judges.
options.viewport: Schedule cover, set off-centre: 'Highland Creative · Schedule of Classes · Est. 1985', with a live entry tag on a string (pick a class, name, phone) and tap-to-call. Sections numbered down the side as navigation.
options.risk: Tips into country-fair kitsch if the wood type and ribbons are overused; it has to stay a working studio site.

raised.raise: A live 'Gates open' line shows whether the Mittagong studio is open right now, from real business hours.
Asymmetry as law: the schedule sits off-centre and tags hang at their own angles, with no centred hero.
Every section opens with its own numbered section card before its classes, like a bumper.
Form states print themselves as a steward's stamp ('ENTRY RECEIVED · No. 0412'), not toast chrome.

options.label: The Typesetter's Proof
options.lineage: 1985 job tickets, galley proofs and printer's specimen books
options.thesis: The studio's hand-drawn-and-typeset origin, shown as a live proof sheet to approve.
options.viewport: A press sheet with crop marks around the hero, a job ticket filled in with the enquiry, and plum and olive swatch strips along the bleed.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: print-proof hairlines and mono labels are where most runs in this category land.

options.label: Made to Measure
options.lineage: home sewing pattern envelopes and tissue
options.thesis: Every service is a pattern with views A, B and C, and the back of the envelope says what's included.
options.viewport: Envelope front: three service views lettered A/B/C; pick one and its cut line turns solid; yardage-style table of inclusions on the back.
options.case: Fuses well on clarity (service tiers map to views; the chosen line turns solid). Weaker on audience: reads hobby-craft for a business studio.
options.risk: Pattern tissue drifts toward a beige craft-shop look if the red isn't committed.

options.label: The Showground Fence
options.lineage: fly-posted festival flyers on a country hoarding
options.thesis: Bowral's event posters pasted layer on layer, with one calm white enquiry panel on top.
options.viewport: Full-bleed paste-up of seasonal posters; 'CREATIVE' with one colour per letter; a white finder card with the enquiry.
options.case: Locals know show posters on the fence (holds audience). Loses on clarity for a 40-year studio pitch.
options.risk: Loud; can read as a festival rather than a considered studio.

options.label: Saturday Title Card
options.thesis: Steven and Helen's caricatures as the stars of the show.
options.viewport: Starburst card with the logo bowed across it.
options.case: Their own caricatures fit, but it reads childish and hides the offer.
options.kept: Each section announced by its own card.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.viewport: Soot-black ground with a glowing vessel.
options.risk: Moody and off-brand for plum and olive.
options.case: No link to the studio or its clients.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The studio as a text-mode BBS.
options.viewport: ANSI title screen with numbered menu.
options.risk: No one in the audience identifies with it.
options.kept: Scarce live presence (is the studio open now?).

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The enquiry as a typed dialogue.
options.risk: Cold and technical for a warm family studio.
options.kept: System states print themselves instead of appearing as chrome.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern design-studio site: seasonal hero, portfolio grid, testimonials, contact, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed seasonal tree, big headline, two buttons, then services and a work grid.
canonCard.risk: Polished but indistinguishable from every other studio site.
